html:
The Dane-zaa, called the Beaver by fur traders, are an Athabaskan people of the Peace River country in northeastern British Columbia and northwestern Alberta.

They hunted moose, caribou and beaver on the forests and prairies of the Peace, moving in small bands. In the 1700s the Cree, armed with guns from the fur trade, pushed them west. The North West Company built Rocky Mountain Fort near today's Fort St. John in 1794, one of the first European posts in what is now British Columbia, and the Hudson's Bay Company took over later. Dane-zaa bands signed Treaty 8 in 1899 and 1900. Their dreamers, prophets who were said to travel in dreams, are well known. Oil, gas and dams have since changed much of their land.
sum: The Dane-zaa, called the Beaver by fur traders, are an Athabaskan people of the Peace River country in northeastern British Columbia and northwestern Alberta.
